panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Panel A provides clear histological evidence (GMS/PAS stain) of fungal form invasion in a patient diagnosed with chronic invasive fungal rhinosinusitis. B: Panel B provides clear histological evidence (GMS/PAS stain) of fungal form invasion in a patient diagnosed with chronic invasive fungal rhinosinusitis. C: Panel C shows the H&E stained section of the lesion, demonstrating chronic inflammation and fibrosis which are key features of chronic invasive fungal rhinosinusitis, even if the specific findings are not in the vocabulary.

in_text_mentions: Histologically, the slides were stained with Haematoxylin and Eosin (H&E), Periodic acid-Schiff (PAS), and Gomori Methenamine-Silver (GMS). One week after debridement, the results of H&E, PAS, and GMS-stained were available. Investigation of H&E, PAS, and GMS-stained sections showed invasion of fungal hyphae into submucosa surrounded with evidence of chronic inflammation and fibrosis in the lesion (Figure 2).

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: The panel shows an H&E stain of the maxillary sinus demonstrating broad, aseptate fungal hyphae and clear evidence of angioinvasion, consistent with chronic invasive fungal rhinosinusitis as per the caption and article context. B: The panel shows an H&E stain of the maxillary sinus, displaying fungal elements (broad, aseptate hyphae) and evidence of angioinvasion within the necrotic tissue, confirming the diagnosis of chronic invasive fungal rhinosinusitis.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: MR image showing aggressive orbital extension of chronic invasive fungal rhinosinusitis, specifically extension from the left maxillary sinus through the orbital floor. B: MR image showing the extent of the orbital complications of chronic invasive fungal rhinosinusitis, including enhancement and swelling of the left orbital soft tissues.
panels.attribution_text: Suri et al. From delay to diagnosis: Chronic invasive fungal rhinosinusitis presenting with facial and orbital complications.. Clinical case reports 2023. doi:10.1002/ccr3.7600. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: MR brain images. These images shows enhancing inflammatory phlegmon (left image) extending from left maxillary sinus through orbital floor and involving intraconal orbital fat, the optic nerves, optic nerve sheath, and left orbital apex (right image). Additionally, there is an abnormal swelling and enhancement of the extraocular muscles of the left orbit.
in_text_mentions: ribution, and a hard palate fistula with erosion into the left maxillary sinus. A detailed ENT examination and biopsy found that there was copious green inspissated crusting in the anterior nasal cavity with evidence of a necrotic inferior and middle turbinate. Frozen sections of the inferior and middle turbinate were taken that (on initial read) did not show fungal elements. Further imaging (shown in Figure 1) showed left maxillary sinusitis with extension into the maxillary sinus walls, palate, infratemporal fossa, and left orbit (with involvement of the optic nerve and extraocular muscles).
